newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bank results seen slipping in H2 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italian bank results seen slipping in H2 1996.

text.p: Italian banks are expecting "less favourable" second half results than those seen in the first six months of 1996, the head of the Italian Banking Association told reporters on Tuesday.
Tancredi Bianchi said banks had benefited in the first half of 1996 from a jump in the value of their bond holdings, adding that this sharp climb had not been repeated in the second half of the year.
A study of 173 Italian banks showed a combined net profit of 2.09 trillion lire in the first six months of 1996 against 900 billion lire in the same period last year, ABI said.
